question: Given $M=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $N=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$. Prove that $\det(MN)=\det(M)\det(N)$. Calculate $\det(MN)$ by direct computation and by property, and compare.
explanation:
First compute determinants of $M$ and $N$.
$\det(M) = 4\cdot3 - 0\cdot1 = 12$.
$\det(N) = 2\cdot2 - 5\cdot1 = 4 - 5 = -1$.
Thus $\det(M)\det(N) = 12(-1) = -12$.

Now compute $MN$.
$MN = \begin{bmatrix}4\cdot2+1\cdot1 & 4\cdot5+1\cdot2 \\ 0\cdot2+3\cdot1 & 0\cdot5+3\cdot2\end{bmatrix}$.
$= \begin{bmatrix}9 & 22 \\ 3 & 6\end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $\det(MN)$.
$\det(MN) = 9\cdot6 - 22\cdot3$.
$= 54 - 66 = -12$.

Both methods give $-12$.
Hence $\det(MN) = \det(M)\det(N)$.
